background.source: One Hundred Years of Solitude, written by the renowned Colombian author Gabriel García Márquez, takes readers on a journey through the multi-generational story of the Buendía family. The novel focuses on the founding of Macondo, a fictitious town, by the patriarch, José Arcadio Buendía, and its subsequent history spanning across a century. One Hundred Years of Solitude is considered a remarkable representative of the literary Latin American Boom of the 1960s and 1970s, which was inspired by Modernism and the Cuban Vanguardia literary movement. García Márquez's use of magical realism style and thematic substance adds to the novel’s allure, making it one of the most important contributions to the Hispanic literary canon, as well as to world literature. With its translation into 46 languages and over 50 million copies sold, One Hundred Years of Solitude is, without a doubt, García Márquez's magnum opus and a must-read for literature enthusiasts.
background.target: Into the Wild is a compelling true story that follows the life of Chris McCandless, who abandoned his comfortable life and ventured into the Alaskan wilderness with little more than a backpack and some basic supplies. As he journeys into the wilderness, McCandless met a variety of people, including Jon Clark, who shared his survival philosophy and a desire for adventure. Despite the warnings of the Clark family and others, McCandless remained determined to follow his own path, and he ultimately faced a series of challenges that tested both his physical and mental limits. This film offers a captivating glimpse into the transformative power of nature, as well as the complex and often conflicting motivations that drive people to explore and seek out new experiences. Whether you are a fan of survivalism or simply looking for an inspiring story of human resilience, Into the Wild is a must-see film that will leave you with a newfound appreciation for the power of adventure and the beauty of the natural world.
